newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: PRESS DIGEST - Netherlands - PRESS DIGEST Sept 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Netherlands - PRESS DIGEST Sept 3.

text.p: Following are some of the main stories in the Dutch newspapers this morning.

HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD - Public spending watch-dog says there are problems with four subsidized government schemes for reintroducing long-term unemployed into the workforce. (p1) - Unilever is weighing major shake-up involving about 20 pct of its activities. (p1) - Majority of Houtgroep Nederlands shareholders wants to block takeover by rival Eecen. (p1) - Cable maker Twentsche Kabel books 14 pct H1 net growth to Dfl 22 million from Dfl 19.3 in same period of 1995. (p3) - Brewer Brand, a Heinken unit, is ready to double its sales. (p3) - Property fund Wereldhave mulls sale of property on Carnaby Street in London. (p5) - Shipowner KNSM Kroonburgh, owned by Nedlloyd, is to accelerate sales of its fleet in order to lease ships in future. (p5) - Energy and retail concern SHV seeks heavy expansion of its coal activities. (p5)

DE VOLKSKRANT - Cabinet seeks to compensate houseowners for higher property-tax, resulting from new valuation by local councils. (p1) - Tax-deductabliity of pension premiums to be limited in future. (p3) - Chemicals concern Akzo Nobel's board chairman C. van Lede wants compulsory education for the company's staff. (p7) - Small and medium-sized businesses are very optimistic about economic outlook. (p17)

DE TELEGRAAF - Starch producer Avebe to start large-scale production of environment-friendly fully degradeable substitute for plastic next year. (p1) - Two suspects in BolsWessanen insider trading case say they overheard information in their restaurant. (p1) - Computer salesman Willem Smit is back in automation with new company InterNOC. (p23)
TROUW - U.S. Chemical giant Exxon to extend its Rotterdam Botlek plant. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD - Shoe importer Van Vliet Groep to cooperate with Achten group. (p11) - Fast growth of number of tele-workers. (p11) -- Amsterdam newsdesk +31-20-504-5000
